title: Settings
subtitle: Settings apply to new work. A job that is already running keeps its own settings.

analysis.vocabularyHint: One per line: names, nicknames, slang and game terms that appear often. They guide recognition only – nothing is replaced automatically.
analysis.timingRepair: Align subtitle timing to the speech
analysis.timingRepairHint: Checks each subtitle word against the audio: no word appears before the speaker starts or stays after they stop, with no overlaps and no flicker. Sentences the recogniser 'heard' in silence are removed. The words themselves never change.
analysis.forcedAlignmentHint: Quality mode only. Finds exactly where each word is spoken, using an extra model. Needs an optional install (backend/requirements-alignment.txt, about 1 GB). If it isn't installed, the audio-based alignment above is used.
analysis.cloudFallback: Cloud second opinion for uncertain subtitles
analysis.cloudFallbackHint: Quality mode only, with an OpenAI key saved on the server. Only the few seconds around an uncertain sentence are sent, not the video. A correction is accepted only when it matches another recognition or is clearly more certain; nothing is written by AI.
analysis.profileHint: Fast: for a computer without a graphics card; on long videos, visual analysis runs only on the candidate moments. Quality: for an NVIDIA GPU; full analysis. Automatic chooses by hardware.
analysis.longSource: A video counts as long from
analysis.longSourceHint: In fast mode, visual analysis of a long video runs only on the moments chosen as candidates.
analysis.sensitivityHint: High sensitivity finds more moments, including average ones. Low picks only the standout ones.
analysis.sampleFpsHint: More frames give a more precise analysis and a longer processing time.
analysis.padBeforeHint: Seconds kept before the moment itself
analysis.chatHint: Requires authorized access to the chat data. When there is no data, the signal simply has no effect.
analysis.modelHint: A larger model is more accurate and needs more memory and time

models.auto: Automatic (recommended) – fast: small + re-check of unclear parts; quality: strongest model
models.turbo: large-v3-turbo – accurate and faster than large (~1.6GB)

analysis.whisperMissing: faster-whisper is not installed. Transcription will not run, and jobs will continue with audio and video signals only, without subtitles.
analysis.firstDownload: The first time, the model is downloaded from the internet and stored locally. After that you can work offline.
analysis.noTranscript: Without transcription no subtitles are created, and moments are chosen by audio and video signals only.

editing.howBody: The editing engine decides where to cut dead air, where to change the frame size and when to speed up. That is the difference between a segment cut out of a stream and one that feels edited. The style is set separately for long clips and for shorts.
editing.removeSilenceHint: Turning this off keeps every silence in place, in every style.
editing.angleHint: A slight change of frame size on every cut. Without it, cuts look like jumps.
editing.minGapHint: 0 = follow the style. Silence shorter than this is not cut.
editing.maxRemovedHint: 0 = follow the style. The largest share of the clip that may be removed.
editing.dramatic: The editor never cuts a silence detected as dramatic – a pause followed by meaningful speech is part of the moment, so it is shortened instead of removed.
editing.musicFileHint: Full path to a file on the computer running Polixor. The app does not supply music – bring a file you have the right to use.
editing.presenceHint: Loudness is measured against the music file itself, so the same choice sounds the same with every file.
editing.musicNote: The music ducks automatically under speech and rises at the emotional peak. It is added after voice processing, so the voice reaches its loudness target regardless of the music.
editing.captionsOff: Subtitles are turned off in the Subtitles tab.

director.title: AI director
director.plan: Build an edit plan before executing
director.planHint: The director analyzes the structure – hook, context, emotional peak, call to action – and only then decides what to cut, where to reframe and which words to emphasize. Every decision is stored with its reason.
director.off: With the director off, editing is done by the earlier heuristic editor: dead-air removal and tightening, without understanding the structure of the video. This is normal behavior – just less smart.
director.pacingHint: Sets how often something changes. Within each style the role is tuned: an emotional peak gets more air, an opening less.
director.captionPresetHint: All presets run on the same engine – the parameters change, not the mechanism.
director.rawNote: The “Raw” editing style turns the director off completely – it is an explicit request for a straight cut without editing, and it overrides the settings here.

auto.label: Follow the editing style
auto.hint: Derived from the style chosen above. The default.

clean_creator.label: Clean creator
clean_creator.hint: A change every 3–6 seconds. Professional and restrained.

podcast_clip.label: Podcast clip
podcast_clip.hint: A change every 3.5–7 seconds, with subtitles.

educational.label: Educational
educational.hint: A change every 3–5.5 seconds, more illustrations.

product.label: Product
product.hint: A change every 2.5–4.5 seconds, focus on the product.

cinematic_story.label: Cinematic story
cinematic_story.hint: A change every 5–9 seconds. Slow and emotional.

auto.label: Follow the pacing style
auto.hint: Derived from the style the director chose. The default.

clean.label: Clean
clean.hint: Two quiet lines at the bottom, no animation.

viral.label: Viral
viral.hint: One line, up to three words, running highlight.

cinematic.label: Cinematic
cinematic.hint: A small, restrained caption. The picture comes first.

podcast.label: Podcast
podcast.hint: Breaks at every speaker change, a color per speaker.

story.label: Story
story.hint: A short caption in the middle of the frame.

director.masterHint: Measures the clip after rendering, decides what is needed, applies it and measures again. A source that already meets the target is left untouched.
director.targetHint: The integrated loudness the clip is brought to. If the result misses the target, the clip is marked “Needs review” and the original audio is kept.

social.label: Social media
social.hint: -14 LUFS. The platforms normalize there anyway.

podcast.label: Podcast
podcast.hint: -16 LUFS. The common standard for long listening.

director.denoiseHint: Applied only when noticeable background noise is measured in pauses. With no pauses there is no measurement, so no reduction is applied.
director.compressHint: Applied only when the gap between peaks and speech is too large.
director.destructive: Audio processing is destructive: noise reduction softens the voice and compression removes dynamics. So each step runs only when measurement shows it is needed, and clipping from the recording is reported, not “fixed”.

clips.maxCountHint: A ceiling, not a target: only moments that pass the quality bar become clips.
clips.qualityBarHint: Higher = fewer, stronger clips. A weak video can return few clips or none; the selection report lists the near misses.
clips.llmJudge: Second opinion from the language model
clips.llmJudgeHint: When an AI provider is connected, it reviews the top candidates: it can only rank a clip slightly up or down or reject a weak one – it never writes or changes text.

longModes.continuous: A continuous stretch of the stream
longModes.highlights: A compilation of the best moments

clips.layoutBlurHint: Nothing is cropped from the frame and the picture stays sharp, because the center is not enlarged.
clips.layoutFaceHint: Face tracking relies on detecting frontal faces; if none are found, a center crop is used.

layouts.blur_pad: Full frame on a blurred background

clips.hwNone: No hardware encoder detected; the CPU will be used.
clips.normalizeHint: Evens out the difference between quiet speech and shouting. Turn off to keep the original audio.
clips.exportDirHint: Leave empty to use the app's default folder.
clips.concurrentHint: More than one job needs a lot of CPU and disk.

subtitles.title: Subtitles
subtitles.scope: These settings apply to live-stream jobs and older jobs. Projects have their own subtitle designer with a live preview, in the project's settings step.
subtitles.wordLevelHint: Available when the transcription returns word timings. Otherwise subtitles are shown per sentence.
subtitles.fontHint: For Hebrew, choose a font that supports Hebrew. If the font is not installed, Polixor picks a suitable fallback automatically.
subtitles.titleCard: Title card at the start of the video
subtitles.titleCardHint: Shows the clip title in the first seconds.
subtitles.fromTranscript: Subtitles come from the transcript only. Before exporting you can correct any line in the clip editor.

modes.cloud: Cloud model – requires an API key

ai.heuristicNote: This mode always works, offline and free. Titles and descriptions are derived from the transcript and from audio/video signals, so the wording is less polished than a language model's and understanding of story context is limited.
ai.ollamaNote: Requires an Ollama server running at http://localhost:11434 and a model pulled in advance (ollama pull). No data is sent to the internet. Result quality depends on model size, and a large model needs memory and a GPU to run in reasonable time.
ai.cloudNote: In cloud mode, transcript excerpts are sent to an external service. The key is stored encrypted on your computer and is never exposed in the browser.
ai.discover: Let the model suggest quiet moments
ai.discoverHint: The model reads the transcript and looks for interesting moments that are not loud, which audio signals miss.
ai.cookiesNote: A cookies file you exported yourself from your browser allows downloading content your account is permitted to watch. Polixor does not access your browser and does not bypass DRM, age, region or paid-content restrictions.

images.title: Image creation
images.openaiNote: The prompt is sent to OpenAI from the server only. The key is stored encrypted on your computer, is not part of the browser code and is never returned by the API except as a mask.
images.placeholderNote: This provider creates a graphic card on your computer. These are not AI images, and they are labeled as such everywhere in the interface. It exists so you can test inserting images into video without an API key.
images.retriesNote: A retry happens only on a temporary failure – quota exceeded, timeout or an unavailable service. A rejected prompt or a missing key is not retried.
images.serverOnly: Every call to the image service goes out from the local server only. The API key is stored encrypted on your disk, is never exposed in the browser and is not part of the interface code.

live.title: Live stream capture
live.segmentNote: The recording is saved in segments. A shorter segment reduces how much material is at risk if the process crashes, but adds seams.
live.maxMinutesNote: 0 = recording continues until you stop it or the stream ends.
live.keepHint: Useful for recovery if merging fails. Takes extra disk space.

system.benchmarksNote: The ratio is processing seconds per second of stream. Time estimates in the interface are based only on these measurements.
system.noBenchmarks: Not enough measurements yet. Until they accumulate, Polixor shows no completion estimate – instead of guessing.
system.cleanupNote: Deletes extracted audio, transcripts and analysis data of finished jobs. Source files and clips are kept.
